name: FOCAS Lab
full_name: Formal Control and Autonomous Systems Lab
intro: We design controllers for robots and cyber-physical systems that come with formal guarantees: robust, reliable, and safe by construction. Our work spans theory and hardware, from temporal-logic specifications and spatiotemporal tubes to learning-based control and multi-robot systems.
address: FOCAS Lab, Department of Cyber-Physical Systems
TCS Smart X Hub, Indian Institute of Science

research.title: Spatiotemporal Tubes
research.text: Our flagship approach. A spatiotemporal tube is a time-varying region the system must stay inside; we design tubes that avoid obstacles and reach targets on deadline, and a closed-form controller that keeps the system in the tube, with no model approximation and no online optimisation.
points: Prescribed-time reach–avoid–stay tasks with a formal guarantee
Static, moving and uncertain unsafe sets, updated in real time
Unknown dynamics and input constraints, from Euler–Lagrange robots to articulated vehicles
Applications beyond robotics, such as a provably safe artificial pancreas
repos: Real-time STT for dynamic unsafe sets

research.title: Temporal Logic & Resilience
research.text: Complex missions such as “visit A within 4 s, then B, and never enter C” are written in signal or linear temporal logic. We synthesise controllers that satisfy these specifications by construction, and measure how much disturbance or energy loss a system can absorb before a task fails.
points: Controller synthesis for the full class of signal temporal logic (STL) tasks
Resilience metrics and maximally resilient controllers
Assume–guarantee contracts for interconnected systems
Reinforcement learning made tractable with tube-shaped STL rewards

research.title: Learning with Guarantees
research.text: Many systems have no reliable model. We learn controllers and safety certificates from data, then verify them, so a learned policy comes with a proof (or a probability bound) rather than only good test results.
points: Neural control barrier functions and neural stabilising controllers
Physics-informed networks that learn spatiotemporal tubes
Fast, sample-efficient verification with extreme learning machines and graph neural networks
Certified sim-to-real transfer via simulation-gap functions; Gaussian-process funnel control

research.title: Multi-Robot Systems
research.text: Robot teams must hold formations, stay connected and avoid each other using only what each robot can sense. We build distributed controllers with safety guarantees that scale with team size.
points: Formation tracking with a single control-barrier-function constraint
Safely acquiring a rigid communication graph under limited sensing range
Socially aware navigation for unknown multi-agent systems
Prescribed-performance multi-cluster consensus
repos: STT for socially aware multi-agent systems

research.title: Stability & Symbolic Control
research.text: Cyber-physical systems mix discrete switching with continuous dynamics. We study incremental stability (all trajectories converging towards each other), which makes symbolic abstractions and compositional controller design possible for large systems.
points: Incremental stability of switched and interconnected systems
Neural and learned controllers with incremental-stability guarantees
Symbolic abstractions and compositional synthesis
Scalable verification for large-scale networks

research.title: From Demonstrations to Robots
research.text: Every method is tested on real hardware: mobile robots, manipulators, drones and an F1TENTH car in a motion-capture arena. We also teach robots from human demonstrations, including imperfect ones, while keeping the safety guarantees.
points: Robust imitation learning from mixed-skill demonstrations
Learning from demonstration inside spatiotemporal tubes
Safe trajectory tracking with moving obstacles, validated on planar robots
Open-source ROS / ROS 2 stacks for the lab's robots

openings.title: PhD / M.Tech (Research)
openings.text: Apply to the Department of Cyber-Physical Systems through IISc admissions. Windows open in March–April and September–October.

openings.title: Postdoctoral research
openings.text: For PhD holders, including those who have submitted their thesis, with experience in control, robotics, formal methods, ML or RL. Funding routes include the IoE / C. V. Raman PDF, NPDF and DS Kothari fellowships.

openings.title: Research internships
openings.text: For undergraduates in EE, ECE, CS, ME, robotics or applied mathematics. The INSA Summer Research Fellowship and FAST-SF usually open in October–November.
